Updated July 19, 2026, 6:17 p.m. ET

For the first time in Men's or Women's World Cup history, there is a back-to-back Golden Boot winner.

France's Kylian Mbappe, helped along by a two-goal performance in the third-place game against England on Saturday, July 18, was able to edge out Argentina's Lionel Messi and win the honor of the World Cup's leading goal scorer, netting 10 goals to Messi's eight.

The two were neck-and-neck in both goals and assists at eight and four, respectively, heading into the weekend, but an offensive exhibition between England and France that ended in a 6-4 win for England ultimately proved to be the difference.

Mbappe and Messi were in a head-to-head chase in the 2022 World Cup as well, with Mbappe finishing with eight goals to Messi's seven. Messi, however, got the last laugh, with Argentina defeating France in penalty kicks to win the World Cup championship.

2026 World Cup Golden Boot final tally

The Golden Boot is awarded to the player with the most goals scored at the World Cup. Ties are broken by the player, or players, with the most assists. Further ties are broken by the player, or players, with the fewest minutes played.

The 2026 World Cup is a wrap!

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the final on Sunday, July 19 in East Rutherford, N.J.

Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute. It was his first goal of the 2026 tournament and third World Cup goal overall.

Not only was the winning side crowned on the final day of the month-long competition, but there were several other awards that were given out. Spain had a solid day, nearly sweeping the individual trophies along with their second World Cup title.

Heading into the finale, Lionel Messi was in the race for the Golden Boot, the trophy given to the leading goal-scorer of the tournament, but he failed to score in the loss. Argentina, who was hoping to defend their 2022 World Cup win, had zero shots on goal in the match.

Here are the winners of the 2026 World Cup player awards:

Rodri, Spain - Golden Ball (best player in the tournament)

Spain's Rodrigo Hernández Cascante, better known as Rodri, has been awarded the Golden Ball for the 2026 World Cup as the best player in the tournament.

The captain of La Roja orchestrated a midfield that authored six clean-sheet victories, including in the final. In the semifinal match Rodri won 11 duels, more than the entire French midfield, to propel Spain to the final.

He is the 11th player to win the World Cup, Champions League and Ballon d’Or.

Kylian Mbappé, France - Golden Boot (most goals in the tournament)

Unai Simon made history in this World Cup even before the final kicked off. Now he has the hardware to go with it.

The Spain goalkeeper won the Golden Glove as the best goalkeeper at the 2026 World Cup on Sunday, July 19, capping a tournament during which he allowed one goal in eight matches and set records that had stood for decades.

search_result.title: Do goals in World Cup third-place match count toward Golden Boot?
search_result.text:
July 18, 2026, 7:02 a.m. ET

The World Cup Golden Boot race is a tight one.

Kylian Mbappé is tied with Lionel Messi with eight goals and Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham aren't far behind with six each in the competition for most scores at the global tournament.

The problem is, the France star and England duo are not playing in the final. They will instead face each other in the third-place match on Saturday, July 18.

Messi and Argentina beat the Three Lions 2-1 in their semifinal match. France was denied a third straight trip to the final when Spain beat them 2-0 in the other semifinal.

Mbappé and Kane have each won the Golden Boot at previous tournaments. Mbappé took home the trophy in the 2022 World Cup with eight goals after losing to Argentina in the final. Kane captured the title in 2018 with six goals when England finished fourth. Each player won the Golden Boot with the amount of goals they have heading into their last match of the 2026 competition.

Messi will have his chance to capture the Golden Boot in the final against Spain on Sunday, July 19.

Does the World Cup third-place match count toward the Golden Boot award?

Yes! Goals in the World Cup third-place match count toward the Golden Boot.

Therefore, Mbappé, Kane and Bellingham have a chance to win the award for most goals in the tournament.

Messi and Mbappé are tied with eight goals throughout the competition. Kane and Bellingham each have six.

What happens if there's a tie in goals for the Golden Boot at the World Cup?

If multiple players are tied in the Golden Boot race at the end of a World Cup, the winner is decided by whoever tallied the most assists to go with their goal count.

If the Golden Boot were to be decided as it stands with both Mbappé and Messi tied at eight goals each, Messi would win his first Golden Boot because he has four assists compared to Mbappé's three.

Has anyone won the Golden Boot with a goal in the World Cup third-place match?

Yes! According to BBC Sports, there have been four players who won the World Cup's Golden Boot after scoring the deciding goal in the third-place match.

Jáminton Campaz put the exclamation point on Colombia's win over Uzbekistan with his first goal of the tournament. Cucho Hernández was under pressure in the corner and struck the ball to Campaz in the corner of the goal box, who knocked in a perfect header.

Uzbekistan's celebration at scoring its first World Cup goal was cut short when Luis Díaz scored his first goal of the tournament moments later. He took the assist from Gustavo Puerta and struck the ball past goalkeeper Utkir Yusupov into the net.

Harry Kane, who won the 2018 Golden Boot with six goals, started his 2026 World Cup campaign with a goal in England's group play match against Croatia. It was a retake of a penalty kick.

Yoane Wissa, who plays for Newcastle United, scored a historic goal for DR Congo as the equalizer against Portugal. It was the national team's first ever goal in a World Cup.

search_result.title: Why the University of Tennessee is suing Claude AI creator Anthropic
search_result.text:
Updated July 21, 2026, 8:52 p.m. ET

The University of Tennessee Research Foundation is suing AI company Anthropic for alleged patent infringement.

The lawsuit claims Anthropic infringed on two UT patents related to neural networks without permission.

UT is seeking monetary damages and an order to stop Anthropic from using its patented technology.

This is reportedly the first patent infringement lawsuit filed against the company behind the AI program Claude.

The University of Tennessee System's nonprofit research arm is suing Anthropic, an artificial intelligence company it says violated two UT patents related to neural networks inspired by the human brain.

Neural networks, according to IBM, "are among the most influential algorithms in modern machine learning and artificial intelligence." The technology "stacks simple 'neurons' in layers and learns pattern-recognizing weights and biases from data to map inputs to outputs."

The complaint, filed by the UT Research Foundation, seeks to protect the professors behind the technology and their contributions to innovations developed and put into practice "years before artificial intelligence systems became widely deployed in commercial products and services."

Anthropic, which operates the popular AI program Claude, recently agreed to a $1.5 billion settlement in a class-action copyright lawsuit brought by authors who alleged their work was used to train AI systems. A California judge approved the settlement July 20.

That same day, the UT Research Foundation filed its federal lawsuit against Anthropic in Delaware, where the company is based.

"We disagree with the allegations and intend to defend this case vigorously," a spokesperson for Anthropic told Knox News via email.

The UT Research Foundation since 1935 has worked to protect, manage, license and enforce intellectual property rights for research and inventions across all five UT campuses, including the flagship campus in Knoxville. Knox News could not immediately reach the foundation for comment.

UT's patents, according to the complaint, have contributed to artificial intelligence, machine learning, neuromorphic computing and neuroscience-inspired computing fields through years of research.

"Anthropic’s cavalier approach to others’ intellectual property rights in the development of its products extends beyond the use of copyrighted material," the complaint said.

Other companies such as Apple, Google and Microsoft have cited UT's patents when pursuing their own patents for related technologies.

UT is asking for unspecified monetary damages and for the court to block Anthropic from infringing on its patents. The lawsuit, according to reporting by Reuters, is thought to be the first patent infringement case against Anthropic.

search_result.title: Christopher Nolan's 'Odyssey' debut breaks major box office record
search_result.text:
Updated July 19, 2026, 1:42 p.m. ET

Is Christopher Nolan the most reliable director working today? With his latest film, the Oscar winner has pulled off a feat that few filmmakers can.

Nolan's "The Odyssey," a nearly three-hour epic based on the classic poem by Homer, is officially a hit at the box office: It opened to a massive $124.5 million in North American theaters, according to studio estimates released by Rentrak on July 19.

This sets a new record for Nolan as the director's biggest opening weekend at the domestic box office for any of his films that aren't sequels, meaning the largest outside of his "Dark Knight" trilogy. That record was previously held by "Oppenheimer," which launched with $82.5 million domestically in 2023.

"The Odyssey" also debuted with $264.1 million globally, the biggest worldwide opening weekend of Nolan's career.

Join our Watch Party! Sign up to receive USA TODAY's movie and TV recommendations right in your inbox

Need a news break? Check out the all new PLAY hub with puzzles, games and more!

That "The Odyssey" nabbed a bigger debut than "Oppenheimer" is especially impressive, given the latter movie benefited from the "Barbenheimer" phenomenon: Fans paired Nolan's J. Robert Oppenheimer biopic with "Barbie" in a double feature, which was believed to have boosted both movies at the box office.

No such pairing existed with "The Odyssey," though the film boasted a star-studded cast that included Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Robert Pattinson and Anne Hathaway. But the most important star may have been Nolan himself, who in recent years has become one of a handful of directors whose name alone can sell a movie. His last two films, "Oppenheimer" and "The Odyssey," have both managed the kind of blockbuster openings typically reserved for franchise movies.

"The Odyssey," in fact, had a larger opening weekend than the latest entries in the "Star Wars," "Minions" and DC Universe franchises. Its debut ranks as the second biggest of the summer movie season, behind only "Toy Story 5," and the third biggest of the entire year, behind "Toy Story" and "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie." For live-action films, "The Odyssey" had the biggest domestic debut of 2026.

In an unusual move, tickets for select screenings of "The Odyssey" went on sale in July 2025, a full year before the movie's debut, and quickly sold out. Tickets for IMAX 70mm screenings were particularly in demand, in part because "The Odyssey" made history as the first major studio movie to be completely filmed using IMAX cameras.

"The Odyssey" is likely to do big business throughout the summer, as fans who were unable to snag IMAX tickets on opening weekend see it in subsequent weeks.

And even after the summer ends, the conversation around the movie is sure to extend into 2027: "The Odyssey" is widely expected to be a major player at next year's Academy Awards, just three years after Nolan's "Oppenheimer" dominated the Oscars in 2024, winning seven awards, including best picture.

How 'The Odyssey' opening compares to other Christopher Nolan films

With "The Odyssey" added into the mix, here's a look at the opening weekend for all of Nolan's films to date, excluding his early movies "Following" and "Memento," which did not receive wide theatrical openings, and "Tenet," which was released during the COVID-19 pandemic, when movie theaters were shut down in much of the U.S.. The numbers, via Box Office Mojo, are not adjusted for inflation.

search_result.title: IMAX 70mm showing 'The Odyssey' in 2 Texas theaters. Here's where
search_result.text:
July 23, 2026, 11:16 a.m. ET

Christopher Nolan's new film, "The Odyssey," is best viewed in IMAX 70mm, the director's intended format.

Only 25 theaters in the United States are equipped to show the movie in IMAX 70mm.

"The Odyssey" is the first narrative feature film to be shot entirely with IMAX cameras.

Tickets for these limited screenings are in high demand, with some selling out a year in advance.

Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" is drawing moviegoers eager to experience the film the way the director intended — on an IMAX 70mm screen. But that experience is only available at a handful of theaters nationwide.

Just 25 theaters across the United States are equipped to project the film in IMAX 70mm, including only two locations in Texas. That means many fans may need to travel to see the movie in one of the highest-quality theatrical formats available.

With "The Odyssey" now playing in theaters, here's where Texans can find IMAX 70mm screenings, what makes the format different and what other premium viewing options are available.

What is 70mm IMAX?

In the simplest terms, 70mm IMAX is the way to see "The Odyssey" both in the highest resolution and on the largest screen possible.

Need a news break? Check out the all new PLAY hub with puzzles, games and more!

A standard film strip is 35mm, so 70mm film is physically larger, resulting in a higher-resolution picture. Showing the movie in IMAX allows for an expanded image. So by seeing "The Odyssey" in 70mm IMAX, you're seeing more of the frame than you would in a normal theater, and the image itself also looks better.

This is how Nolan recommends watching "The Odyssey," but securing a seat in one of those screenings, particularly on opening weekend, will be tough. The tickets are so in demand that 70mm IMAX screenings started going on sale in July 2025, one year before the movie's release. At the famed Lincoln Square IMAX theater in New York City, even showings at 3 a.m. are fully sold out.

What's special about seeing 'The Odyssey' in 70mm IMAX?

Nolan has shown his films in 70mm IMAX before, including his most recent movie, "Oppenheimer." But "The Odyssey" marks a historic first, both for Nolan and for movies in general: It's the first narrative film to be shot entirely using IMAX cameras.

Typically, films will shoot only select sequences in IMAX, because IMAX cameras are loud, bulky and expensive. The cameras make so much noise that it has been difficult to film dialogue in this format, which is why most movies have only used IMAX cameras for big action sequences.

But with "The Odyssey," Nolan solved this by placing the camera inside a casing dubbed a "blimp" to reduce noise, allowing him to film both action and dialogue scenes for IMAX while maintaining the expanded frame throughout the entire movie.

Dallas − Cinemark Dallas & IMAX, 11819 Webb Chapel Road

San Antonio - AMC Rivercenter 11 & IMAX, 849 E Commerce St., Suite 800

search_result.title: Is going to the movies still worth it? Tell us. | Opinion - USA Today
search_result.text:
July 16, 2026, 2:10 p.m. ET

I love going to the movies.

I love going alone or with my friends. I love walking into my local AMC and being greeted by a familiar face as the worker guides me to my theater. I love sitting in a room full of strangers, itching with anticipation for the experience we’re about to share. I love watching previews and mentally marking which films I’ll be coming back for. I love watching Nicole Kidman, in that iconic pinstripe pantsuit, recount that “indescribable feeling we get when the lights begin to dim” and remind me that “heartbreak feels good” at the movies. Because it does.

And I’m not alone.

Members of Gen Z – born between 1997 and 2012 – are now the most frequent cinemagoers, with 87% saying they have seen at least one film in a cinema in the past 12 months, according to a Fandango survey.

This summer, horror flicks "Obsession" and “Backrooms” are drawing Gen Z audiences and seeing meteoric success. “Obsession” recently achieved another box office milestone, clearing more than $400 million in global ticket sales as of July 16. “Backrooms,” an adaptation of director Kane Parsons' viral YouTube short film series, landed the biggest box office opening in A24 history, with $81.4 million. Christopher Nolan’s highly anticipated adaptation of “The Odyssey” broke BFI Imax records with $1 million in ticket sales in the first 24 hours back in June.

For many Gen Zers, the movies act as one of the last, and most ubiquitous, “third places” left standing. Having such a communal space is key to fighting America’s loneliness epidemic across generations.

With all that being said, movie theaters aren’t perfect. Like literally everything else, the price of going to the movies has increased.

In 2016, the average movie ticket was $8.65. Today, a standard evening ticket at AMC costs $13.99, and that's before you factor in fees and premium formats like Dolby, IMAX or 3D, which can run upwards of $50 (“The Odyssey” was shot entirely in IMAX.) Overpriced concessions also dig deeper into our pockets.

Streaming services have changed the way we consume films. Because of the hefty cost of going to the movies, audiences must decide if seeing a certain film is worth footing the bill or waiting until it comes out on streaming.

Do you go to the movies? Tell us below.

So, how do you decide if a movie is worth trekking to the theater or waiting for the streaming release? What are the best films to see in theaters? When was the last time you went to the movies? Did you go alone or with a group of friends? Do you think movies have gotten too expensive? Do you use Letterboxd to log films you’ve seen? Will you see “The Odyssey” in theaters?

July 7, 2026 Updated July 8, 2026, 3:43 p.m. ET

Christopher Nolan has done it again.

The first reactions to the Oscar-winning director's latest movie "The Odyssey," a star-studded adaptation of the epic poem by Homer, have arrived, and they're through the roof.

On X, Next Best Picture Editor-In-Chief Matt Neglia said the highly anticipated film is "as epic as movies get," adding that it has "some of the most breathtaking set pieces" Nolan has ever attempted and is a "colossal achievement of scale."

IndieWire Editor at Large Anne Thompson wrote that her "high expectations were met" with the "stunningly mounted" film, which she declared is the movie "to beat" for best picture at the 2027 Oscars. "Matt Damon could win best actor and a bevy of supporting thesps and noms will follow."

Join our Watch Party! Sign up to receive USA TODAY's movie and TV recommendations right in your inbox

Need a news break? Check out the all new PLAY hub with puzzles, games and more!

Los Angeles Times film editor Joshua Rothkopf praised the movie as "staggering" and "pure cinema," writing, "Obviously the story is about returning home, but in a larger sense, this is also a return home to the robustly entertaining action movies that cinema was invented to tell."

Polygon Deputy Editor Jake Kleinman wrote on X that while "The Odyssey" is Nolan's "most straightforward movie ever," it's "also maybe his most impressive," noting that "both the epic scale and attention to detail are absolutely stunning. The closest comparison I can think of is Peter Jackson's 'Lord of the Rings' trilogy."

Variety Senior Artisans Editor Jazz Tangcay hailed the movie as an "astonishing achievement," and a "triumphant, spectacular epic," adding that the cast delivers some of "the best performances of their career."

"The Big Picture" host Sean Fennessey kept it simple: "I liked THE ODYSSEY."

Several of the early reactions also highlighted the film's surprising horror influences. The Hollywood Reporter Film Editor Aaron Couch observed that the film "gives us a first: a fleshed out horror sequence directed by Christopher Nolan."

Matt Damon stars in the lead role of Odysseus in "The Odyssey" alongside a stacked cast of costars including Tom Holland, Zendaya, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o and Charlize Theron.

The film has been highly anticipated ever since it was announced as Nolan's follow-up to "Oppenheimer," one of the biggest success stories of the "Inception" director's career. The 2023 biopic about the "father of the atomic bomb" was a surprisingly huge hit for an adult drama driven largely by dialogue. Thanks in part to fans pairing it in a double feature with "Barbie," "Oppenheimer" grossed nearly $1 billion worldwide, and it became Nolan's first movie to win the Oscar for best picture. Nolan also won best director.

Anticipation for "The Odyssey" has been so high, in fact, that screenings began selling out a full year in advance: Tickets for select IMAX showings went on sale, and were quickly snatched up, in July 2025, before filming on the movie had even been completed.

"The Odyssey" hits theaters on July 17.

Movie theaters couldn't be happier as the new "Wicked" brings some magic back to the 2025 box office.

"Wicked: For Good," the second film in the two-part movie adaptation of the hit Broadway musical, made its debut with a strong $150 million in North America this weekend, according to estimates from Comscore.

The haul surpasses the $112.5 million domestic launch of the original "Wicked" movie, meaning "For Good" has set a new record for biggest opening weekend ever for a film based on a Broadway show. The record was previously held by the first "Wicked."

"Wicked: For Good" also snagged the second-biggest opening weekend of the year in North America. It came in a bit below "A Minecraft Movie," which opened with $162.7 million in April, but above "Lilo & Stitch," which took in $146 million in its first three days of release. The Disney live-action remake hit theaters over the long Memorial Day weekend and debuted with $182.6 million, including Monday grosses.

Join our Watch Party! Sign up to receive USA TODAY's movie and TV recommendations right in your inbox

Need a news break? Check out the all new PLAY hub with puzzles, games and more!

Cynthia Erivo and ​​Ariana Grande reprise their Oscar-nominated roles of Elphaba and Glinda, respectively, in "For Good," which picks up where the Broadway show's second act starts and wraps up the characters' stories while tying into the events of "The Wizard of Oz."

Critics were generally more mixed on "For Good" than the first "Wicked," but audience reception appears to be comparable to the original. Moviegoers polled by CinemaScore gave "Wicked: For Good" an average grade of A, the same rating as 2024's "Wicked."

But movie theaters won't have to wait long for more blockbusters, with the sequel to the animated smash hit "Zootopia" set to open Nov. 26 for Thanksgiving weekend, almost a decade after the original Disney movie grossed more than $1 billion globally. That will be followed soon after by the highly anticipated "Avatar: Fire and Ash," James Cameron's second sequel to the highest-grossing film of all time, 2009's "Avatar."

Though another direct "Wicked" sequel isn't expected, the cast may still have one last stage where they can say goodbye to the two films: the 2026 Oscars. The first "Wicked" received 10 nominations at the Academy Awards, and since "For Good" features two new original songs that are eligible for awards consideration, it could surpass that number.
